agree.reason: The nurse's first-hand numbers and the plain way the piece faces the objections will win over undecided parents, but a parent with an 8 a.m. shift or a board member worried about sports gets sympathy and a request for 'a plan' rather than a solution, so they may not be moved.

honest.reason: The piece declines the brief's request to promise a higher graduation rate and says outright that the neighboring district hasn't proved it, and its ratios are accurate; the small stretches are 'each one a class a student wasn't in' and the unsourced line about teen body clocks.

works_the_facts.reason: It turns the brief's raw figures into vivid true forms: more than twice either later period, nearly three in four students, and one in six not graduating on time; it does little more with the attendance point or the $180,000, such as a per-student or per-day cost.

right_comparison.reason: The status quo is set out fairly as a cost borne by most students every morning against costs borne by some families some of the time, which matches the facts, though the brief has no trend data to go further.

qualification.reason: The commitment to report tardies, attendance and nurse visits after one year, and graduation after the first full four-year class, can be checked, but it gives no target numbers and the only consequence of a miss is that 'the board will know it.'

objections.reason: All three objections are named and given weight, but the after-dark practices and the drop-off problem are answered by comparison and by handing them to the district rather than by anything concrete, and it raises no objections the brief already settles.

fit.reason: It is a well-built op-ed of roughly 630 words, under the 650 limit, with a headline, a clear ask tied to the April 14 vote, and a byline placeholder.
